question: How did adult flu vaccination change at each clinic between seasons?
audience_and_claim: Clinic managers; uptake rose at all three clinics, most at North

critique_of_draft.problem: The title says reminder texts caused the rise, but the table only shows that uptake rose, and it rose at South and East too.
critique_of_draft.repair: Use a descriptive title: uptake rose at all three clinics, most at North.

critique_of_draft.problem: The y-axis starts at 50%, so North's 12.5% rise is drawn as a 117% rise (lie factor 9.3).
critique_of_draft.repair: Start the bar axis at zero with ax.set_ylim(0, 100).

critique_of_draft.problem: The y-axis has no label, so readers cannot tell the values are percentages of adult patients.
critique_of_draft.repair: Label the axis "Adults vaccinated against flu (%)" and write each value on its bar.

critique_of_draft.problem: Only red versus green separates the seasons, a pair many colorblind readers cannot tell apart.
critique_of_draft.repair: Use colorblind-safe colors plus a different hatch for each season.

critique_of_draft.problem: Thick black edges, a heavy grid, and the same hatch on every bar carry no data.
critique_of_draft.repair: Drop the edges and grid, hide the top and right spines, and keep hatches only where they mark the season.

text_alternative: Grouped bar chart of adults vaccinated against flu (%) at three clinics in the 2024-25 and 2025-26 seasons, on a 0 to 100% axis. All three rose: North from 56% to 63%, South from 57% to 60%, and East from 61% to 62%. These are clinic records only; they do not show that North's reminder texts caused its larger rise.
